Follow live updates here. 50,000 Americans are receiving $5,000 payments, IRS says: Do you qualify?
 Leada Gore Mon, October 26, 2026 at 12:25 PM MST 2 min read The Internal Revenue Service is sending $5,000 refunds to a select group of 50,000 Americans. The refunds are related to a specific tax credit for adoptions and a change in tax laws. 
 Here's what you need to know: 
 Why are people receiving refunds? 
 The Internal Revenue Service has begun issuing refunds related to carryforwards from the adoption tax credit due to a change in the Working Families Tax Cut law. The money comes from unused tax credits families carried forward because their tax bills were too small to absorb them. 
 Prior to the change, adoption tax credits carried forward could only offset any taxes that were owed. For lower-income families that didn't owe taxes, the adoption credit could sit unused for years. 
 The change applies to the 2025 tax year only. 
 Who qualifies? 
 To qualify, you must: 
 Have carried an unused adoption credit from 2020 through 2024 into 2026 
 Filed your tax return before April 15, 2026. 
 Is every adoptive filer eligble? 
 No, according to the IRS. 
 "You may not receive an adjustment if you already received the correct refundable adoption credit, if you do not have adoption credit carryforwards available for use in 2025, or if the IRS does not have enough information to make the adjustment because, for example, you did not file a federal income tax return for tax year 2025 or have never claimed the adoption credit despite being eligible to do some," the IRS said. 
 How much are the refunds? 
 Refunds are capped at $5,000 per adopted child. 
 "This adjustment may result in a refund, a reduced balance due, or no change in the amount owed or refunded, depending on the taxpayer's account," the IRS said. 
 Do people have to request the refunds? 
 No, eligible people will receive refunds automatically. No amended tax return is required. 
 When will people receive refunds? 
 The IRS said they expect the refunds to be complete by the end of the year. Eligible taxpayers will receive a notice from the IRS within 30 days of the adjustment to let them know the amount they will receive and if it was applied to another tax or non-tax debt.
